title: First brass band parade and pay
summary: Robinson recalls his first street parade on carnival day, the pay, and walking the route.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you play with a brass band in different range? No. Did you ever play with any brass bands here in the city?
The city? Yeah. Oh, you know that Dick.
I know, but I want you to tell me.
What ones? What was your first brass band you ever played with? I'll put it that way.

The first brass band I played with. See the New Orleans? That was on the carnival day, Budapetit. Budapetit on the carnival day. And that was the first parade I played too. Budapetit. With old man Parker, Willie Parker.
Buddy was playing the trumpet. Yeah.

Upright. Upright, yeah. That was the first band I played with. I mean on the street. I didn't want to take it then. Did that understand? I wasn't thinking about the music. I didn't want to take it then. Money wasn't much. It was only ten dollars. Who were you playing for?
Playing for Jefferson and Budapet. You didn't have to walk for it, did you? Walked for it.

Walked for the Oliverton Park down the Connox Street and went on and walked up back up there again. That's not the way out. Well, I was a young man then too. I was young. But I can't see. That's why the folks asked me now. But playing in parades. I don't mind taking the parade for it. Not a parade. I mean a little parade for church to pray.
